issues.legal_issue: A reservation of land lapses when, after the prescribed long period of reservation and service of a valid release notice, the land is neither acquired nor the formal acquisition declaration is published within the notice period.
material_facts: The land remained reserved for a public purpose under the revised development plan for more than ten years without acquisition proceedings being completed.
The owners served a notice seeking release of the land from reservation, and the authority received it on 19 March 2002.

Within six months of the notice, an improvement committee recommended acquisition and the Chief Engineer sent communications concerning acquisition. The Municipal Corporation later authorized its Commissioner to apply for acquisition, but no application by the authorized Commissioner was produced.
No acquisition declaration was published within the six-month period, which expired on 18 September 2002. The State Government published its declaration on 20 November 2002.
issues.conclusion: The reservation was deemed to have lapsed, the land was released from reservation, and the owners could use it for development as otherwise permissible for adjacent land under the relevant plan.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 126 and 127 of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966 must be read together. Under Section 127, after the specified period has elapsed and a valid notice is served, acquisition or commencement of the steps for acquisition must occur within the ensuing six months. The steps must be steps towards acquisition that can result in acquisition, not merely preliminary recommendations or requests for time. For acquisition through the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, publication of the declaration under Section 6 is the necessary commencement of acquisition proceedings; a request to the State Government to acquire the land is not enough. The provision safeguards owners against indefinite reservation and must be construed to give effect to that purpose. The Court relied on Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay v. Dr. Hakimwadi Tenants’ Association, 1988 (Supp.) SCC 55, and statutory-interpretation principles in Collector of Customs v. Digvijaysinhji Spinning & Weaving Mills Ltd., AIR 1961 SC 1549; His Holiness Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala, AIR 1973 SC 1461; Narashimaha Murthy v. Susheelabai, (1996) 3 SCC 644; American Home Products Corporation v. Mac Laboratories Pvt. Ltd., AIR 1986 SC 137; Tirath Singh v. Bachittar Singh, AIR 1955 SC 830; Commissioner of Income Tax v. J.H. Gotla, AIR 1985 SC 1698; and State of Rajasthan v. Leela Jain, AIR 1965 SC 1296.

rule.if: reserved_land_acquisition_case and prescribed_reservation_period_elapsed and owner_served_valid_release_notice and not land_acquired_within_notice_period and not formal_acquisition_declaration_published_within_notice_period

predicates.reserved_land_acquisition_case: The proceeding concerns land reserved for a public purpose in a planning scheme and the acquisition of that land.
predicates.prescribed_reservation_period_elapsed: The applicable period for acquiring the reserved land or commencing acquisition proceedings had elapsed.
predicates.owner_served_valid_release_notice: The landowner or another interested person served a valid notice seeking release of the land from reservation.
predicates.land_acquired_within_notice_period: The reserved land was acquired within the period following service of the release notice.
predicates.formal_acquisition_declaration_published: The government published the formal declaration commencing acquisition within the period following service of the release notice.

issues.definition: When reserved land remains unacquired beyond the applicable reservation period and, after a valid release notice, is neither acquired nor made subject to a formal acquisition declaration within the notice period, the reservation lapses and the land is released for otherwise permissible development.

issues.legal_issue: Observations in an earlier decision about acquisition steps are not binding precedent on an issue that the earlier case did not decide.
material_facts: The earlier case concerned when the period following a landowner’s notice began to run, including whether it began only after the owner supplied requested information.
The earlier case did not require the Court to decide what steps an authority had to take to commence acquisition after receiving a notice seeking release of the land.
The observations in that decision linking acquisition steps to steps contemplated by the relevant acquisition provision were not necessary to resolve the earlier case.
issues.conclusion: The earlier observations about what constitutes steps for acquisition after service of a release notice were not part of the ratio decidendi and did not bind the Court in deciding that issue.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 141 of the Constitution, the binding part of a decision is its ratio decidendi: the principle applied to the material facts to decide the issue before the Court. Observations on an issue not requiring decision are obiter and do not become binding merely because they appear in a judgment. The Court relied on Quinn v. Leathem, 1901 AC 495; State of Orissa v. Sudhansu Sekhar Misra, (1968) 2 SCR 154; Additional District Magistrate, Jabalpur v. Shivakant Shukla, (1976) 2 SCC 521; Union of India v. Dhanwanti Devi, (1996) 6 SCC 44; Director of Settlements, A.P. v. M.R. Apparao, (2002) 4 SCC 638; and Shin-Etsu Chemical Co. Ltd. v. Aksh Optifibre Ltd., (2005) 7 SCC 234.

predicates.precedent_interpretation_case: The court is deciding whether observations in an earlier judicial decision bind it on a legal issue.
predicates.earlier_case_did_not_require_deciding_th: The issue now before the court was not necessary to resolve the earlier case.
predicates.earlier_observations_were_not_necessary_: The earlier court’s observations on that issue did not form a necessary basis for its result.

issues.definition: When an earlier case did not require resolution of an issue and its observations on that issue were unnecessary to its result, those observations do not bind a court deciding that issue.
